Incentives for establishing Fabs  in
India
*41. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
would introduce special package of
incentives for establishing Fabs in India;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government are considering a proposal on
electronic and IT hardware manufacturing
policy; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Vacant posts in Postal Department
†*42. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the number of employees
in the Postal Department is continuously
decreasing;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) the number of posts lying vacant at
present, category-wise and the progress
made in filling up these posts; and
(c) whether the work of postal service
is being affected due to the vacant posts in
the department and the courier services are
flourishing?
Assessment of the projected demand
for mobile handsets
*43. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made any
assessment of the projected demand for
mobile handsets in the wake of growth in
mobile telephony in the country; if so, the
details thereof;
(b) whether ITI manufactures GSM
mobile handsets;

16
(c) if so, whether the capacity is
sufficient to meet the projected demand;
(d) if not, the reasons therefor;
(e) whether ITI proposes to take up
the poduction of compatible mobile
handsets to meet the increasing demand for
affordable handsets in view of the growing
value added services;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) if not, the reasons therefor?
Master Plan of Delhi
†*44. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Master Plan of Delhi
has been published;
(b) whether an assessment has been
made about the population of Delhi in the
year 2021 and the housing requirement for
the same;
(c) whether stress has been laid in the
Master Plan to maintain the status quo;
(d) whether this would encourage
construction of multi-storey buildings
which would make other basic amenities
such as water, sewage, road, parking, etc.
unmanageable; and
(e) whether it would be ensured that
the multi-storey buildings already
constructed or to be constructed would
be fully earthquake-proof?
Revision of royalty on coal
†*45. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some States
have demanded immediate hike in royalty
on coal;
(b) if so, the decision taken by
Government in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that these
States have demanded that the rate of
royalty should be based oon the value of
coal and not the quantity; and
(d) if so, Government's decision in this
regard?
Road development plans
*46. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Centre
propose to develop 7,603 km of road links
in the NE region;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action plan of the Centre for fast
development of road infrastructure in the
KBK region of Orissa, (the most backward
region of the country) to improve its
economy?
Rural BPO centres
*47. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether NASSCOM has estimated
that the Indian BPO sector is likely to face
a shortfall of more than 2,50,000 IT
professionals by the year 2012;
(b) if so, whether Government would
explore expanding the rural internet kiosk
project, which offers a lower cost of
operation while employing IT skilled
workforce living in rural areas;
(c) whether the IIT Chennai has been
working on a model rural BPO initiative; and
(d) if so, the number of rural BPO centres
which are now operational under this
scheme?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Radio-active material stolen from
CMPDI
261. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a container
packed with radioactive material was stolen
from Jharkhand's Central Mine Planning
and Development Institute (CMPDI);
(b) whether it carried Uranium and could
have an adverse effect in an area of 1.5
kilometres;
(c) whether it is also a fact that it was
stolen from densely populated town of
Rajrappa, which was sent from a federal
atomic facility near Mumbai;
(d) the quantity of Uranium stolen and
how highly is this Uranium enriched; and
(e) what would be its impact both
physically and mentally on the local
population, if it finds way into rivers,
rivulets or food chains?
Private investments in atomic power
generation
262. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there are any proposals
before Government to invite investments
in atomic power generation;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of regulatory mechanism
being adopted in this sector?
Uranium availability in the country
263. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether in the wake of recent 'Indo-
US Nuclear Agreement' signed between the
two countries, Government propose to
initiate a complete 'review' on the present
availability of Uranium in the country,
required for peaceful use of nuclear power;
(b) if so, the details of the quantity of
Uranium available in the country, State-

63
wise particularly in 'ROHIL' in Rajasthan;
and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
fuel our Nuclear Power Plants, till date?
Increasing power generation with
atomic fuels
264. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
increase power generation with atomic fuels;
(b) if so, the proposed investment
requirement for per MW Unit of atomic
energy;
(c) whether Government undertook any
cost benefit analysis of atomic power
generation in comparison with that of coal,
hydro, naphtha and other such fuels;
(d) if so, the findings thereof; and
(e) if not, whether Government would
undertake such an exercise before finalizing
investment proposals for atomic power
generation?
Increasing power generation through
NPC
265. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are expecting
to increase power generation with atomic
fuels;
(b) if so, the investment requirement
according to the generation target;
(c) whether Government are increasing
the investment through Nuclear Power
Corporation; and
(d) if not, the plans contemplated to
meet the expenditure?
Attainment of self-sufficiency in
nuclear power production
266. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Nuclear Power
Corporation of India (NPCI) proposes to
add nuclear power capacity of 50,000 MW
by 2032;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) how far this would help to attain
self-sufficiency in power production in the
country?
Merchant Power Plants
267. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose
to allow Merchant Power Plants' by
accepting the proposal of captive blocks
allotments;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of captive coal blocks
awarded so far and power generation added
consequent to that?
Power generation by CII
†268. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Coal India Ltd. has
any plan to step in the field of power
generation;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the units of the Coal
India Ltd. which have been included in this
scheme?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
